parsed.title: Nephrology referral: rapidly declining eGFR in diabetic kidney disease — Willie Norbert Klocko (DOB 1967-07-05)

sections.heading: Reason for referral
sections.text: I am referring this 59-year-old man with type 2 diabetes, diabetic kidney disease and proteinuria for urgent nephrology assessment because of a steep decline in renal function over the past twelve months, now accompanied by symptoms that could represent uremia. He was seen at urgent care on 2026-08-19 and reviewed in my office on 2026-09-11 for fatigue and nausea. At that visit he reported about three weeks of fatigue, poor appetite and nausea most mornings, without vomiting. The problem is still carried in the chart as chronic kidney disease stage 3, which no longer matches the most recent filtration estimate.

sections.heading: Renal trajectory
sections.text: Over the window 2025-08-19 to 2026-08-19 the eGFR fell from 55.45 on 2025-09-10 to 15.6 on 2026-08-19, a 71.9% decline of roughly 0.53 mL/min per week. Whole-blood creatinine rose over the same period from 1.62 to 5.7, having been 3.69 in May and 4.4 in late July, so the slope has been steepest in the last six months. Potassium was 4.2 and BUN 17 on the most recent panel, both without alarming features.

sections.heading: An unresolved laboratory discrepancy, and why I have not restaged
sections.text: The two creatinine series disagree at the same timepoint. Serum creatinine on 2026-08-19 was 1.9408, essentially unchanged from 1.8853 a year earlier (+2.9%), while the whole-blood creatinine drawn the same day was 5.7. BUN is also flat at 17.25 against a baseline of 16.39, which I would not expect alongside a true creatinine of 5.7. A system proposal to restage the problem as CKD stage 4 was declined: it rests on a single whole-blood value, and I want a repeat serum creatinine from a single laboratory before the problem list is changed or further renally cleared doses are adjusted. The clinical picture nonetheless concerns me enough that I do not want to wait on the restaging question before you see him.

sections.heading: Suspected contributors and what has been changed
sections.text: Naproxen 500 mg twice daily was started around 2025-10-01 for bilateral knee osteoarthritis, and the creatinine rise follows that start: 1.62 on 2025-09-10, 4.5 by late November 2025 and 5.7 on 2026-08-19. The patient told me he was not aware this was a problem for his kidneys; I have recorded the NSAID as a suspected contributor and it has been stopped as of 2026-09-11, with counselling against over-the-counter NSAIDs. He remains on lisinopril 10 mg daily and as-needed furosemide 40 mg, which compound the hemodynamic risk of an NSAID in advanced CKD; hydrochlorothiazide was stopped on 2026-09-11 and the evening insulin dose was reduced by 4 units at the same visit. He also carries a diagnosis of hypotension, which limits how aggressively I can manipulate the diuretic and ACE inhibitor without your input.

sections.heading: Metformin — decision deferred
sections.text: Metformin 500 mg remains on the active medication list despite an eGFR of 15.6 on 2026-08-19, which is well below the threshold at which it is contraindicated for lactic acidosis risk. He is already on isophane/regular human insulin, so glycemic cover would be preserved if metformin were held, and his three weeks of nausea and poor appetite add to the concern. I have held this decision pending the confirmatory serum creatinine rather than stopping it on a single discordant value, and would act immediately on your advice.

sections.heading: Relevant background
sections.text: His problem list includes type 2 diabetes with diabetic kidney disease, microalbuminuria and proteinuria, essential hypertension, metabolic syndrome, ischemic heart disease, chronic congestive heart failure, anemia, hypertriglyceridemia and nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy, the last reviewed at an ophthalmic examination on 2026-09-09. Cardiac medications are clopidogrel 75 mg, simvastatin 20 mg, metoprolol succinate 100 mg, amlodipine 2.5 mg and as-needed nitroglycerin.

questions: Given the discordance between serum creatinine 1.9408 and whole-blood creatinine 5.7 on 2026-08-19 with a flat BUN, how would you like the true level established — a single repeat serum creatinine and BUN at your laboratory, or cystatin C / measured clearance — and how soon do you want to see him regardless of that result?
Should metformin 500 mg be stopped now on the strength of the eGFR of 15.6, or held pending the confirmatory creatinine, with insulin alone providing cover?

With naproxen stopped, do you want lisinopril 10 mg daily continued for its proteinuria benefit, or reduced/held given the fall in filtration and his documented hypotension? Same question for the as-needed furosemide.
If the advanced-CKD picture is confirmed, would you take over anemia and mineral-bone workup and begin discussion of renal replacement planning and access, and what should I monitor in the interim?
